summary: CERTIFIED census of all 2,880,504 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 through 10^8 finds 14 K(p)=∞ cases, so the proposed universal polylog-level assertion is false for this certificate subfamily (not for ES). Finite cumulative maxima at 10^2,...,10^8 are 5,20,40,557,23105,23105,41027; the last is at 85664329, while 184837 attains the exact boundary (p+3)/8=23105. Seven-point log K versus log log bound slope is 7.326 (R²=.905), changing to 8.984/10.487 when early decades are removed, not a stable polylog law. All 14 distinct data/lsa/hard.txt primes and 43 selected records/tails were independently factored, plus all 609 primes through 10^4; see BRAINSTORM/z52d_pass2_ZF0_part2.md §Z3167.
not_done: No extrapolation beyond 10^8 or fit treating infinite K as finite; no full-Type-II replacement of the deficient subfamily.
next: Study finite record tails separately from the 14 structural zeros, or replace the subfamily by full Type II.

summary: EVIDENCE: evaluated K(1,1;p) for all 39,175 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 through 10^6 against actual unordered ES counts U(p), replacing pass1’s truncated R_K proxy. Spearman is +.003261 raw and +.005623 after dividing K by sqrt(p); matching p mod840 and 100000-wide size bins gives rank correlation +.007591 with 1000-permutation p=.1459. Five size-bin correlations range from −.00414 to +.00981; 30 independent complex-sum checks agree. No pointwise correlation signal emerges at this range.
not_done: No p ≡ 3 mod4, primes beyond 10^6, or other Kloosterman frequencies.
next: No follow-up indicated for this specific null test.

summary: PROVED replacement (memo §Z1597): for S_z(C)=sum_{q≤z,q∤4p}1[q|4Cp+1], A=sum 1/q and m=#q, the mean square is ≤A+(m²+2Am)/X, hence ≤A+3/sqrt(X) at z=X^(1/4); for A>5 this bounds the poor fraction by (A+3/sqrt(X))/(A−5)², uniformly in p. The requested unrestricted full-omega bound centered at log log(Xp) is false by CRT plus Linnik, and no Brun-strength bound is claimed. CERTIFIED: all 4,783 primes p ≡1 mod4 through 10^5, C≤4096 give 104,472 rich levels (omega≥6), 103,748 of them failures; even restricting to feasible 8C−3≤p leaves 90,252 failures among 90,976 rich levels. Richness alone therefore does not make a level likely to certify in this range.
not_done: No uniform full-omega variance theorem in a restricted polylog(p) regime and no explicit Brun-strength X(log log X)^5/log X bound; the proved small-prime bound is weaker and vacuous at X=4096.
next: Any rich-level forcing argument must control divisor residues, not just omega.

summary: CERTIFIED full minimal-u tabulation for 332,180 primes p ≡1 mod4 through 10^7, with all k at the least u and least-k tie-breaking, finds the 14 genuine no-certificate primes. Finite max u by bounds 10²,...,10⁷ is 2,4,19,78,131,410; the last occurs at (p,u,k,C)=(4160641,410,1269,2), and every finite u≤1.765009(log p)² in this range. Median/90th/99th percentiles of u are 1/2/5, but least k at least u reaches 904004 at p=9944041,u=3,C=1, and median selected C is 234356. Thus the data support small u empirically, not a Siegel-type simultaneous polylog bound on all parameters; see memo §Z1721.
not_done: No theorem extending the observed u envelope, and no optimization of max(u,k,C) over all witnesses.
next: Separate one-coordinate smallness from simultaneous-height optimization and exclude the known empty fibers.

summary:
The pass1 citation EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md concerns U-shift events, not hereditary-property mining for N_e=(p+e)/4. CERTIFIED mining now lists all e=3,7,...,255 with N_e

0, omega(N)≥3) do not imply the e-slice hit; R(N)>0 occurs in 15,408,058 failing slices, while the same N=5 succeeds at (p,e)=(17,3) and fails at (13,7). No hereditary implication is obtained; 3,416 slices receive independent divisor-pair checks.
not_done: No e>255 listing, p ≡3 mod4 census (e=1 is trivial), or exhaustive search over all conceivable hereditary predicates.
next: A viable induction must preserve e-dependent divisor-ratio information, not merely ES(N) or R(N)>0.

summary: No pass2 outcome for Z1477 exists; its pass1 work only checked the gcd identity, not a dependency hypergraph. Built complete shared-prime hypergraphs on C≤1024 for all 4,783 primes p ≡1 mod4 through 10^5, saving explicit hyperedges for six R-zero primes and residue-matched controls. Observed shared-edge co-hits total 56,032 versus 21,138.019 under within-prime 16-level-bin shuffling (2.651×), reduced to 46,943.182 expected (1.194×) under leave-one-out fixed-level propensities matched by p mod840 and 50000-wide size bins. All six zero primes have giant sizes within their ten same-residue controls’ ranges; component/isolate counts also overlap except for a small 23929 outlier, so these summaries do not uniformly distinguish failures (memo §Z2819).
not_done: No claim that all possible graph invariants fail; no fully conditioned probabilistic dependence theorem or formal significance calibration for the co-hit ratios.
next: Test whether the residual co-hit clustering persists after conditioning on more small-prime residues before invoking Janson or LLL.
